value.deck: Microsoft is streamlining its AI portfolio by eliminating underperforming tools like Cortana touchpoints and merging its consumer and enterprise Copilot apps over the next 90 days.
shortVersion: Microsoft has announced that it will discontinue several underperforming AI features, including legacy Cortana integration points and specific Copilot sidebar modes. Alongside these retirements, the company is merging its separate consumer and enterprise Copilot applications into a single, unified experience over a 90-day transition period.

This move aligns with a broader industry shift toward trimming redundant generative AI experiments to focus on centralized, production-ready platforms. For organizations and individual subscribers, the consolidation simplifies the product footprint into a cohesive interface across different user tiers.

The transition creates immediate operational tasks for IT administrators and developers who maintain workflows tied to legacy endpoints. Technical teams must audit their environments before the three-month deadline to avoid disruptions from discontinued sidebar modes and retired integrations.
value.plainLanguage: Microsoft is cleaning up its AI lineup by retiring underused features and merging its separate consumer and enterprise Copilot apps into a single tool over the next 90 days.

value.whyItMatters: It marks a maturation phase in enterprise AI, forcing IT teams and developers to audit their configurations within 90 days while preparing users for a single, unified Copilot ecosystem.
